sentences.text: There is a stand of hornbeam on the east side of the Bela valley where sound behaves oddly, and everybody in Podgora knows it and nobody thinks it is worth mentioning to visitors.
It is about two hundred metres of the path.

You go in under the hornbeams and the valley noise stops — not muffled, stopped — and you walk through a silence that has a texture to it, and you come out the other side and the stream is there again as though it had been switched back on.
The Bela is a loud stream.
It comes down over a bed of flat limestone and it can be heard from the road and from both sets of houses and, on a still night, from the church.
It runs sixty metres from the hornbeam path along the whole of that stretch.
Under the hornbeams it is not there.
Iva had walked it four times a week for the whole of her life to get to the bus, and she had never once thought about it, in the way you do not think about the shape of the doorway in your own house.
She thought about it at twelve because of a school project on acoustics that she had chosen because it seemed easy.
The project was supposed to be about why the school hall was bad for concerts.

Iva had chosen it on the Friday, had realised on the Sunday that she had nothing to say about the school hall, and had gone for the bus on the Monday morning through two hundred metres of silence she had walked through perhaps four thousand times.
She stopped in the middle of it and stood still and was late for the bus.
The books said dense vegetation absorbs sound and the books were right and also nowhere near enough.
Absorption is gradual.
You walk into a wood and it gets quieter over about forty metres.

What happens under those hornbeams happens in about a metre and a half and it happens in both directions, and if you stand with your feet either side of the line and clap, the clap is a completely different object depending on which way you are facing.
Iva stood on that line for most of an afternoon in April with a stopwatch and a phone recording, and by the end of it she had established two things.
The line is not straight and it is not a line on the ground.
It is a surface, roughly vertical, that runs across the path at a slight angle, and she found its position at four different heights by clapping and stepping and clapping again, and it leans.
The first was that the silence was not absorption.
The second was that it was worse in August than in April, and she only knew that because she had walked through it in August all her life and had a body that remembered.
That is not a measurement and she knows it.

She had no April recording from any previous year and no August recording from that one, and the entire basis of the claim, at the time she made it, was that August under those hornbeams had always felt like being underwater and April did not.
She made the recordings that summer specifically to find out whether her body had been right about a thing it had never been asked about.
It had.
